For any caller and any single Put call with value V, the reference contract ensures Acc[caller].balance increases by exactly V (no extra increments from reentrancy), whereas the mutant that fails to set locked_ = true allows reentrant Put to run again and can make Acc[caller].balance increase by more than V for some inputs.

For every caller and any single Put call sending value V, the reference contract always increases Acc[caller].balance by exactly V (no net extra increments), while the mutant that fails to set locked_ = true in the reentrancy guard allows a reentrant attacker to cause Acc[caller].balance to increase by more than V for some inputs.

For every Put call, the reference contract always increments the caller's stored balance before emitting the LogFile entry (so the latest History entry for that caller reflects the incremented balance at the time of logging); the mutant that moves AddMessage earlier can emit a Log entry that observes the old (pre-increment) balance, violating this ordering.

For every call Put(unlockTime) the reference contract always updates the caller's stored balance before the LogFile.AddMessage observable event (so a subsequent read of Acc[caller].balance after Put must be at least the previous balance + msg.value), whereas the mutant that moves AddMessage earlier can produce a Log that observes the old balance ordering and thus can leave the observable stored balance inconsistent with the ordering (i.e., the stored balance may not reflect the deposit at the time of logging).

For every call to Put by any address with any nonzero ether value, the reference contract always increases Acc[caller].balance by msg.value (so address(c).balance and the public Acc mapping reflect the deposit) and does not allow the LogFile.AddMessage to observe a pre-increment state ordering that would leave the contract without the deposited value; the mutant that moves AddMessage before updating acc.balance can produce a Put that returns while the stored balance has not yet been incremented (observable via the public getter/address(c).balance), violating this invariant for some inputs.
